rationale: Y's 'Validated' section explicitly cross-references and confirms resolution of several of the ground-truth's most substantive inline comments (subdir precedence at omni_config.py:1354, omni_kv_config ordering at :1275, diffusion batch-default deferral at :780, and partial coverage of the ownership-validation gap at :838/:901) by naming the specific tests that now guard them, showing genuine engagement with those exact concerns even though the PR has since been fixed. X, while equally rigorous and well-evidenced (both independently catch the same real ROCm AITER dead-code bug, a strong precision signal), pursues a largely disjoint set of issues (ownership over-rejection, scheduler_cls divergence, cache-default layering) that barely overlap with what the human reviewer actually flagged, and neither review touches the top-level #5140-alignment architectural concern. Precision and actionability are comparably high for both — concrete file/line references and specific fixes throughout — so the deciding factor is Y's substantially better recall of the ground-truth concerns.
